summary: Siuslaw NF lookout built 1943 as a 40-ft pole L-4 tower; moved to Cummins Lookout in 1953; no source describes the summit site today.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 40-foot pole tower (creosoted, per the October 1943 newspaper)
facts.status_note: Moved to Cummins Lookout in 1953 per the register and firelookout.com; Forest Lookouts marks the Blodgett site removed; no source describes the site today

events.note: Lookout station under construction in January 1943; workers from Camp Albert Angell were to build a tower (planned as 20 ft in February). By October 1943 a 14-by-14 house on a 40-foot creosoted tower had been erected
Moved to Cummins Lookout in 1953 (register and firelookout.com). Which Cummins site is not identified

corrections.why: The register and firelookout.com both give a 40-foot tower (12.2 m). The current 6.1 m (20 ft) matches only the 20-foot tower planned in February 1943; the October 1943 report describes the 40-foot tower as erected.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: February 1943 reports planned a 20-foot log tower; the October 1943 report and the register describe a 40-foot tower. The story uses 40 feet and mentions the earlier plan.

notes_for_editor: Thin sourcing: three web sources, two of them the same register and firelookout.com pair. The newspaper quotes are all reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page. The identity of Cummins Lookout is unresolved. The Lane County Cummins Peak entry (US 1796, in the record at data/towers/or/us-or-cummins-peak-lane-county.json) gives a 1954 tower and 1975 removal, which does not line up exactly with the 1953 move, so the link is unproven and the story says so. The height correction (6.1 m to 12.2 m) is proposed; the 20-foot figure is the February 1943 plan. A PDF copy of the Forest Lookouts page (orww.org) matches the weebly page. An NRHP nomination for the Blodgett tract turned up in search but was not read; it may help with the tract but is unlikely to describe the lookout.
